description: SpaceTech is a 4-engineer team at NASA Space Apps Konya with TEKNOFEST background. For Earth System Trend Detective, we aim to build and innovate using our proven skills in AI/ML, computer vision, LLMs, and web/mobile development on satellite data. Our team is full; not seeking new members.
summary: Earth Trend Detective is an interactive 3D map app that answers one question from NASA satellite data: "Is the climate really changing here?" Users pick precipitation, soil moisture or air temperature and a region in Türkiye, or click any place on the map. A plain-language decision card then tells them what is changing, how fast, and whether the change is statistically significant, using 25 years of monthly NASA Giovanni data (GPM IMERG, GLDAS, MERRA-2) cross-checked against 45 years of NASA POWER data. For example, it shows that topsoil in the Konya Basin, Türkiye's main grain region, is drying significantly. A chat "detective" agent guides users through the evidence, while every number comes from tested statistics, never from the AI. This turns raw Earth observation data into honest, local answers that farmers, decision makers and students can understand in seconds.
details:
Earth Trend Detective answers one question from satellite data: "Is the climate really changing here?"

WHAT IT DOES

Users pick a variable (precipitation, soil moisture or air temperature) and a region in Türkiye on a 3D map, or click/search any place. A "decision card" then states in plain language what is changing, where, how fast (Sen's slope per decade and in %), and whether the change is statistically significant (seasonal Mann-Kendall test, p-value). If a trend is not significant, it estimates how many more years of data would be needed, or says the trend is too weak to tell. Example finding: topsoil (0-10 cm) moisture in the Konya Closed Basin, Türkiye's main grain region, shows a statistically significant drying trend since 2001.

HOW IT WORKS

- 25 years (2001-2025) of monthly NASA data from Giovanni: GPM IMERG precipitation, GLDAS Noah soil moisture and MERRA-2 air temperature, area-averaged over three study regions (Konya Basin, Eastern Black Sea, Lake Van).

- A 45-year cross-check (1981-2025) with NASA POWER for any point or box in Türkiye, fetched live. When the two datasets disagree, the app says so instead of hiding it.

- A robustness check on yearly means with the Hamed-Rao modified Mann-Kendall test, plus a chart with the raw and deseasonalised series, the trend line and its 95% confidence band.

- Yearly "stripes" show each year's anomaly at a glance; a MODIS NDVI layer (NASA GIBS) gives visual vegetation context; a time player and auto tour walk through the story.

- A chat agent ("detective") answers questions like "Is the soil drying in Gaziantep?" and controls the map. Every number it shows comes from our statistical code, never from the language model. It also works offline in a rule-based mode.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Farmers, local authorities, teachers and students can get an honest, statistically tested answer about climate change in their own area within seconds, without coding or downloading data. The app is transparent: every result links to the exact Giovanni request and dataset, and data can be downloaded as CSV.

TOOLS

Python (pandas, NumPy, SciPy, pymannkendall), FastAPI, MapLibre GL JS 3D map, pytest tests; English and Turkish interface.

LIMITATIONS

Results are regional box averages on ~25-55 km grids, not field-level. Parts of the Black Sea and Van boxes cover water, and this is noted in the app.

USE OF AI

AI coding assistants (Claude Code by Anthropic) were used to help write and review code and documentation; all code was reviewed and tested by the team. The optional chat agent uses a large language model (Groq, Gemini, OpenRouter, Ollama or Claude, selectable) only to phrase answers and choose tools; all statistics are computed by our own code. The project idea and analysis design are the team's own.
